reasoning: The package is a standard binary AUR package that downloads prebuilt tarballs from the official domain (api.fluxer.app) with pinned SHA256 checksums for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The PKGBUILD contains no executable code in global scope, and the package() function performs standard installation operations (extracting to /opt, creating symlinks, installing desktop files and icons). The .SRCINFO and fluxer.desktop files contain only metadata with no executable content. The disagreement between reports was caused by API errors in the qwen model, not by actual security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit .SRCINFO and fluxer.desktop, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files and found them safe. Both models agreed the PKGBUILD was safe. The disagreement is purely a tool failure issue, not a substantive security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO and fluxer.desktop due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: When a model experiences API errors during file review, the audit tool should implement retry logic or fallback to alternative models to ensure complete coverage
Inconclusive verdicts due to tool errors should be distinguished from inconclusive verdicts due to genuine uncertainty about security
When one model successfully completes a full audit and another fails due to tool errors, the successful audit should carry more weight in the final verdict
